title: Sapphire Retail — Fallback Playbook & Integration Sketch
body:
Context and goal:
- Customer: Sapphire Retail (omnichannel grocery chain, ~120 stores + e‑comm).
- Ask from sales: POC to validate resilient query routing for their in-store assistant when the primary high-capacity model (hosted) is overloaded or network is flaky. They explicitly require a documented fallback behavior for compliance and Ops.
- Goal for this doc: working sketch for an internal playbook + integration checklist we can hand to customer SRE/infra for Private or Dedicated rollout. Focus on behavior, constraints, and test plan rather than final config values.

Call summary (2025-11-03, 10:30 PT):
- Attendees: Asha (Redwood), Daniel (Redwood), Marta (Redwood), Theo (Sapphire infra), Priya (Sapphire PM), Jordan (Sapphire SRE)
- Sapphire wants: predictable latency for in-store terminals (SLO 200ms p95 per prompt), ability to degrade gracefully to smaller model variants or cached responses, audit logs for fallbacks, and simple operator controls in their console.
- Key constraints: many stores are on spotty LTE. Edge devices buffer short queries and expect sub-second response where possible; otherwise show canned fallback.
- Compliance ask: all fallback outputs must be logged and marked as "cached" or "degraded" in their internal UI and stored for 30 days.

Primary technical notes / gotchas discovered:
1) Latency vs quality tradeoff:
   - Our hosted LLM p95 for their median prompt length (20 tokens output, 30 token input) measured ~120–150ms in previous benchmarks. That fits. But when load spikes, p95 climbs >500ms.
   - If we route to a quantized small variant (eg. 7B int8), inference time drops but hallucination risk increases on specialized product queries. Need to map which query categories are safe for small-model fallback (price lookup, inventory status) vs ones that must hit a high-quality model (returns policy, legal phrasing).

2) Deterministic labels in responses:
   - Requirement: responses generated via fallback must surface a machine-readable header/field (e.g., "x-rw-source: fallback-small-model") so Sapphire UI can both display a badge and trigger audit retention. Make sure the SDK can pass that metadata back in streaming mode. Streaming headers are tricky — we may need to send final metadata in a trailing event.

3) Cached prefixes and personalization:
   - Many in-store prompts start with identical prefixes ("where is product X in store Y"). Prefix/KV cache can hugely reduce cost and latency but is sensitive to per-store personalization (store IDs, local promos). Cache keys must include store_id and inventory-timestamp. Ops need TTL controls exposed in Console.

4) Network failure modes and local fallback UI:
   - For offline/very-high-latency cases, they prefer: (1) local cached answers (best effort), (2) small-model on local private deployment (if customer opts in for Private), (3) canned message "Try again in a moment". Action: produce SDK sample logic (pseudocode) that tries hosted -> small-hosted -> local-cache -> canned.

5) Tokenization edge case for UPC/barcode-like inputs:
   - Barcode strings and SKU codes sometimes tokenized into many tokens in some model bytepair vocabularies, inflating cost and latency. Recommendation: preprocess to mark these sequences as atomic tokens or pass via embeddings+retrieval pipeline. Include example regex(es) and a pre-tokenization stage in sample code.

6) Cost accounting and alerts:
   - Sapphire wants per-store cost breakout (to feed into internal showback). We'll need to attach route metadata and a store_id tag to every request so Optimize + Console can attribute tokens. Confirm retention window for per-token diagnostics; propose 90 days for debugging then aggregate.

Fallback policies (draft):
- Policy A (Low-latency journaling): for prompts tagged "lookup", route to small-7B-quant if hosted p95 > 250ms OR available concurrency < 20% reserved.
- Policy B (Safety-first): prompts tagged "policy/legal/returns" always route to high-quality model; fallback is to a deterministic canned response + ticket creation if model unavailable.
- Policy C (Offline-first for Private deploy): if Private control plane reachable and local private workers healthy -> route to private-model; else attempt small hosted, else cache.

Integration checklist (high-level):
- [ ] SDK changes: ensure response metadata header for source and fallback_reason in both streaming and non-streaming.
- [ ] Console: expose per-route override for fallback thresholds (latency threshold, concurrency threshold, allowed fallback model list).
- [ ] Instrumentation: ensure store_id and route tags are included in traces; add sample traces to share with Sapphire SRE.
- [ ] Privacy/Audit: add a boolean flag in logs "fallback_used" plus model_id; confirm retention 30 days and field-level encryption for store_id if requested.
- [ ] Evals: prepare a small test suite (100 canonical queries across 4 categories) for regression checks comparing base-model vs fallback-model for correctness/acceptability.

Test plan / POC steps (timeline sketch):
- Week 0: kickoff + share Confluence POC page + access list.
- Week 1: deliver SDK sample and small e2e demo using our hosted fallback chain.
- Week 2: run 1k queries with induced latency spikes to exercise routing; produce metrics (p95, failure rate, fallback rate).
- Week 3: if Private requested, provide image + helm chart for local small-model worker and run in their staging.
- Week 4: share audit log export + operator runbook, ask for sign-off on fallback labeling and retention.

Open questions we need to resolve with Sapphire:
- Which query categories are "safety-critical" (no fallback allowed)? Need their canonical list.
- Do they want fallback labeling visible to end users, or only in operator logs? They currently asked for both.
- Can they accept 30-day retention for fallback logs, or do they need longer (90/365) for compliance?
- Private deploy: do they have HSM/KMS requirements for model keys? If yes, need to schedule security review.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Send sample SDK pseudocode by 2025-11-05. (Asha)
- Ask Console PM for temporary UI toggle to test fallback thresholds (Daniel)
- Create eval prompt set and baseline metrics (Marta)
- Share sample audit export schema and S3 staging bucket details with Jordan at Sapphire (Theo)

Appendix: quick sample pseudocode for client-side routing (sketch)

tryHosted() -> call redwood.generate(route=\"store-lookup\", tags={store_id})
if hosted.p95 > 250 or hosted.errorRate > 0.02:
  // record fallback_reason = \"hosted_slow\"
  trySmallHosted() -> call redwood.generate(model=\"7b-quant\", tags={store_id})
  if smallHosted.success:
     mark response.x-rw-source = \"fallback-small\"
     return response
  else if localCache.exists(key):
     mark response.x-rw-source = \"local-cache\"
     return localCache.get(key)
  else:
     return cannedMessage(\"Currently overloaded; please try again in a few minutes\")

(Will refine this into language-specific SDK snippet once we decide how to surface trailing metadata in streaming.)

Status: draft — want internal review from Console PM + Runtime lead before sending to Sapphire.
